To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a novel in situ/ operando cell that allows for high-pressure and high-temperature studies of catalysts in the synchrotron beam.
a new cell was developed to enable the study of catalysts in the working conditions of a high-pressure catalytic process, the Fischer-Trosch synthesis.

we have designed and built a novel in situ/ operando X-ray diffraction (XRD) cell that is capable of operation at temperatures and pressures typical of high-pressure catalytic reactions, 1373 K and 35 bar, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing and testing the performance of a new synchrotron-based in situ/ operando powder X-ray diffractometry cell capable of operating at elevated temperatures and pressures, 1373 K, and 30 bar, respectively, for the study of catalysts in the working state.
the development of an in situ/ operando cell for high-pressure X-ray diffraction experiments at high temperatures.
the design, development, and performance of an in situ synchtrotron-compatible XRD cell capable of operating at high temperatures and high pressures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cell design is a robust one that is able to provide a high degree of control over the reaction conditions, and that it is capable of delivering high quality data that is suitable for the study of a wide range of catalysts under industrially relevant conditions.
the in situ XRD cell is a robust, versatile and reliable tool for studying high-pressure catalytic reactions.
the in situ cell design is robust and reliable, allowing the in situ characterization of high-temperature, high-pressure reactions, such as catalysis, using synchrotron radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study demonstrates that in situ X-ray diffraction is a powerful tool for studying catalysts in the working state and that the cell design described here can be used to study a range of catalyst systems.
we have developed a high-pressure in situ/ operando X-ray diffraction setup for the Fischer-Tropsh process.
we have developed a novel in situ cell for X-ray powder diffraction studies at elevated pressure and temperature, and have demonstrated its performance using a model catalyst system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed X-ray diffractometer is suitable for studying catalysts at high temperature and pressure, which is important for studying catalysts in their working environment.
the in situ XRD cell can be operated at high pressure, high temperature, and in a reactive atmosphere, which is a unique capability.
it is possible to perform in situ XRD studies of catalysts under high-pressure conditions.
